threads.body: This concurrency key won’t reliably cancel runs created by GitHub merge queue (`merge_group`) attempts, because those runs typically have no `pull_request.number`, and `github.ref` is often a unique queue ref per attempt (so each attempt ends up in a different concurrency group). If these workflows run on merge queue events (as implied by the PR description), consider extending the group expression to also derive a stable identifier from the `merge_group` payload (e.g., a PR number from the merge group’s pull requests list) so newer attempts can cancel older ones.

If `changelog.yml` is triggered by merge queue (`merge_group`) events, the same issue applies: falling back to `github.ref` may create a different concurrency group per queue attempt, so older attempts won’t be canceled. Consider incorporating a stable identifier from the merge group event payload so cancellation works as described in the PR.

threads.body: Same as `ci.yml`: if `check-links` runs for merge queue (`merge_group`) events, `github.ref` may differ for each merge-queue attempt, preventing cancellation of the prior attempt. Consider including a stable merge-queue identifier in the group (e.g., based on PR number(s) from the merge group payload) to achieve the intended runner savings for merge queue churn.
